assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, simple mechanism (interlayer moire hybridisation producing flat bands at a magic angle) predicted analytically, then confirmed by correlated insulators and superconductivity in experiment. It opened a new platform for strongly correlated matter with wide influence on moire physics, and the theory is understood rather than merely observed.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model theory and the Jarillo-Herrero group's experiments are the decisive pair. The first experimental author on the key papers is not in the credited list, and Bistritzer could also be argued for the theory side. Two laureates is the most defensible configuration from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups worldwide, with a rapidly developing but already stable core picture. Timing is good, though the nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
The key experimental first author is not among the credited names, so the allocation of experimental credit is incomplete.
Whether Bistritzer should share the theory credit is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is among the most universal results in non-equilibrium statistical physics, with exact solutions, a connection to random matrices (Tracy-Widom statistics), and quantitative experimental confirmation in liquid-crystal turbulence. It is the kind of surprisingly universal mechanism that appeals to me strongly.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang (with Parisi, who is not in the credited list and whose prior Nobel recognition complicates things) formulated the equation. Takeuchi supplied the decisive experimental confirmation of the universality class. A prize with these three is plausible, but the omission of Parisi and of the mathematical solvers (e.g., Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) leaves the theory credit unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986, the exact solution from about 2010, and the experiments are confirmed by further work in other systems. The picture is mature, though experimental tests of the full universality in diverse systems are still being extended.
uncertainties: Parisi's role and his previous prize may complicate a fair allocation.
Mathematical solvers of the exact KPZ distributions are not among the credited names.
Fraction of real-world growth phenomena in KPZ class remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, enabling the Mott insulator transition, single-site-resolved microscopy and fermionic Hubbard physics. It builds a direct bridge between statistical-physics models and experiment, a lasting new tool for many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Theory of the Hubbard-model proposal (Cirac, Zoller, and others) is credited but the experimental realisations by Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger are the decisive demonstrations. Five credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so a choice is required, and the theory/experiment split is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of confirmation and wide adoption. Largely mature, though quantitative simulation of the open questions (e.g., the fermionic Hubbard pseudogap and d-wave phases) is still ongoing.
uncertainties: Allocation between theorists and experimentalists is difficult with five credited names.
Overlap with the quantum-simulation theory candidate B061 could split recognition.
Quantum simulators have not yet settled the hardest Hubbard-model questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and confirmed the mechanism recognised in 2013. The importance and clarity are very high, and the measurements of its properties have since been stable.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty: thousands of collaborators across two experiments. The credited spokespersons and project founders are plausible representatives, but any choice of three from four is somewhat arbitrary and discards Della Negra, and the Nobel rules do not allow recognising the collaborations themselves.
assessment.maturity: Discovered in 2012 and thoroughly confirmed, so this is fully mature. If it has not been recognised yet, the timeliness concern is the allocation problem rather than the science.
uncertainties: The institutional/collaboration-based credit does not map onto three individuals.
Selection of three from four credited leaders is subjective.
Outside my own research area, so I defer to colleagues in particle physics on credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture gives a unifying, simple account of the rigidity transition in granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses, with critical scaling and a clear connection to isostaticity. It is a statistical-physics concept applicable across many disordered systems, though less sharp experimentally than other candidates.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal of the jamming phase diagram is the identifiable origin, with Liu and Nagel as a natural pair. Subsequent theory by many others (O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Parisi and Zamponi in the infinite-dimensional limit) refined the picture and might dilute the credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely tested numerically and in experiment, but the nature of the transition and its relation to the glass transition remain under active debate, so the picture is not yet fully settled.
uncertainties: The jamming critical exponents and universality are still debated.
Relationship to the glass transition and to the Parisi replica solution is not fully resolved.
Experimental support is more qualitative than for some other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a major field linking band topology to protected edge and surface states; the theory predictions were verified in HgTe quantum wells and in Bi-based three-dimensional materials. Conceptually deep and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group delivered the HgTe confirmation (with theory from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not in the list); Hasan observed the 3D topological insulator. Omitting Mele from the proposed three is a hard choice given the Kane-Mele paper, and B025 overlaps with this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent experiments over fifteen years. Applications are still limited but the science is stable.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) is outside the supplied names.
Dropping Mele is hard to justify scientifically.
Overlap with the quantum spin Hall candidate B025 could split the recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and survey propagation made the statistical physics of disordered systems into algorithmic tools for constraint satisfaction and inference, linking spin glasses to computer science and machine learning. It has a strong conceptual connection to my own interest in statistical mechanics of learning.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Parisi developed the cavity method for spin glasses, and Mézard and Zecchina's work on random satisfiability is the decisive step toward algorithms. Parisi is not in this list and has already been recognised, so the credit in the supplied list is incomplete; Montanari's role is mostly in inference and coding theory.
assessment.maturity: Mathematical validation (e.g., of the Parisi solution) is solid, and algorithmic impacts are well established, but the direct physics breakthrough is arguably already recognised in 2021.
uncertainties: Substantial overlap with the 2021 prize to Parisi weakens the case for a second prize.
The lasting discovery is split between a physics method and computational applications.
Unclear whether practical dominance of the algorithms is established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, using magic-wavelength trapping, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and has transformed precision metrology and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is simple and general and the impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye brought it to the highest accuracy; two laureates are natural. Hall's 2005 prize for frequency combs and the contributions of other groups (Lemonde, Takamoto) are not in the list, but the pair is well supported.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated by many laboratories and used for international comparisons and a pending redefinition of the second, so it is mature or nearly so.
uncertainties: Contributions from other clock groups are not credited in the list.
Prior recognition of frequency-comb work may affect how the committee views novelty.
Whether the redefinition of the second will precede or follow a prize is unclear.
